rows.ARS:
Medium pink Hybrid Tea.
Registration name: Perfume Delight
Exhibition name: Perfume Delight
rows.Origin:
Bred by Swim & Weeks (United States, before 1971).
Introduced in United States by Conard-Pyle (Star Roses) in 1973 as 'Perfume Delight'.
Introduced in Australia by Roy H. Rumsey Pty. Ltd. in 1977 as 'Perfume Delight'.
rows.Bloom: Pink. Strong, damask fragrance. 30 petals. Average diameter 5". Very large, full (26-40 petals), borne mostly solitary, in small clusters, cupped, high-centered bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season. Long, pointed buds.
rows.Habit:
Bushy, upright. Large, glossy, leathery foliage.

Height: up to 4' (up to 120cm). Width: up to 3' (up to 90cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 6b and warmer. Can be used for cut flower or garden. Vigorous. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that.
rows.Patents:
United States - Patent No: PP 3,282 on 2 Jan 1973 VIEW USPTO PATENT
Application No: 165,412 on 22 Jul 1971
Herbert C. Swim and O. L. Weeks, Ontario, Calif., assignors to The Conard-Pyle Company, West Grove, Pa.

...originated by us by crossing the rose variety known as "Peace" (Plant Patent No. 591) with an unnamed and unpatented seedling derived from crossing the rose variety known as "El Capitan" (Plant Patent No. 1,796) with an unnamed and unpatented seedling of "Happiness" (Plant Patent No. 911) X "Chrysler Imperial" (Plant Patent No. 1,167). In the final cross, the variety "Peace" was the seed parent and the unnamed seedling was the pollen parent.
